subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should isolated cron jobs get first-class `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny`, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or continue with only per-job `payload.toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: The choice creates a public security/config boundary for scheduled runs and may change existing announce-mode cron behavior that currently can use the `message` tool directly.

options.title: Add Cron-Scoped Policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence and focused tests for isolated cron delivery modes.

options.title: Inherit Subagent Policy
options.body: Apply `tools.subagents.tools` to cron sessions too, reducing config surface while coupling two different execution modes.

options.title: Keep Per-Job Only
options.body: Avoid a new global cron policy and rely on job `toolsAllow`, docs, and delivery safeguards for scheduled runs.

recommendation.title: Add Cron-Scoped Policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence and focused tests for isolated cron delivery modes.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest combined signal from scoped conversation capability work, current tool-policy pipeline ownership, and prior review context for this issue.
